sections.heading: Review
sections.text:
Vivian is an Ether S-Rank Anomaly Agent whose defining characteristic is her ability to apply extra Anomaly damage based on your other Agents’ Anomaly damage. This element alone makes her fit into several teams and have high flexibility as a Sub-DPS type Agent, it defines the majority of her damage potential and is what her gameplay revolves around. Let’s first explain her kit and mechanics (fair warning: this will be lengthy).
 These “extra Anomalies” (to use simple terms) are called “Abloom”. Vivian triggers Abloom whenever a character is suffering from any Attribute Anomaly of the 5 standard elements (Ether, Electric, Fire, Ice, Physical) and any character in the team uses their EX Special, once per ability used. Simultaneously, Basic Attack: “Featherbloom” is triggered. Featherbloom and Abloom both can activate off-field via any party member’s EX Special attack. This process can also happen whenever any Attribute Anomaly of the 5 elemental kinds is inflicted on an enemy once every 0.5s while her Additional Ability is active. However, in both cases this must come at the cost of 1 “Guard Feather” each time, which Vivian needs to generate on-field in several ways.
 Generating a Guard Feather requires first converting it from a “Flight Feather”. Any available Flight Feathers, up to a maximum of 5, are converted into Guard Feathers via Vivian’s Basic Attack in the “Fluttering Frock” state during which she is suspended in mid-air. Fluttering Frock is activated if any Flight Feathers are available and in the following ways:
 Holding Basic Attack after using Basic Attack 4, Dodge Counter or Quick Assist;

 Using her Noblewoman - Waltz Basic attack (we cover this shortly after);

 Using an EX Special attack, Assist Follow-Up, Chain Attack or Ultimate.

 Holding Dodge cancels the state if it’s undesirable, and can additionally prevent Vivian from causing her to enter this state at all. If at any point Vivian switches out during the Fluttering Frock state, it automatically activates “Suspension” which is the attack responsible for converting Flight Feathers into Guard Feathers. Noblewoman - Waltz is a Basic Attack only available after pressing Basic Attack in the Noblewoman state, during which Vivian gets a free dodge once (which doesn’t give a Dodge Counter). It can be accessed in the following ways:
 After using Basic Attack 4, Dodge Counter or Quick Assist.

 To generate Flight Feathers, which are necessary to convert into Guard Feathers for Vivian to use and trigger Abloom, different abilities give different amounts in the following ways:
 1 Flight Feather after using Noblewoman - Waltz (this gives 1 additional Feather if it triggers a Perfect Dodge);

 2 Flight Feathers after using Chain Attack;

 2 Flight Feathers after using Assist Follow-Up;

 3 Flight Feathers after using EX Special attack;

 5 Flight Feathers after using Ultimate.

 All of these abilities are reliant on Energy of some kind or are slow to access consistently (Noblewoman - Waltz). This means Assist Follow-Ups are especially important to generate Flight Feathers with Vivian. Upon converting available Flight Feathers by using Basic Attack in the Fluttering Frock state (called “Suspension”), Vivian is free to switch out to other characters for them to apply Attribute Anomalies for Vivian to trigger Abloom with.
 Vivian’s Core Passive is responsible for triggering Abloom, and hence it is the top priority to focus on to maximize Vivian’s damage. It has the following effects
 When first engaging in combat, gain 2 Flight Feathers.

 When Basic Attack: Featherbloom hits a target inflicted with an Attribute Anomaly, trigger Abloom which deals damage depending on the Anomaly Proficiency of the inflicted Attribute Anomaly applied to the enemy, as well as the element of the Anomaly (balanced to give out the same damage roughly).

 When Suspension or Featherbloom hit targets suffering any Attribute Anomaly, inflict a Damage Over Time effect called “Vivian’s Prophecy” which deals Ether DMG based on her ATK every 0.55s. This contributes to Anomaly DMG and ends when targets aren’t affected by Anomalies.

 Additional Ability: Corruption and Corruption Disorder DMG increases by 15%. Vivian now also consumes 1 Guard Feather and triggers Featherbloom (and Abloom) up to once every 0.5s when any Attribute Anomaly is inflicted on an enemy.

 Beyond the effects of all abilities listed above, all of Vivian’s combat skills inflict DMG and Daze as normal. Some are Physical DMG, but most are Ether DMG. It is important to level Vivian’s combat skills to an extent for extra Daze output to generate more Stun windows for your team on most enemies, even though only her Core Passive contributes to her Abloom DMG.
 Based on this kit, the game plan with Vivian is therefore as follows:
 Generate up to 5 Flight Feathers in any way (4 is fine depending on the team & available resources);

 Enter Fluttering Frock state;

 Switch out to automatically convert Flight Feathers into Guard Feathers and apply Anomalies to trigger Abloom for lots of Anomaly damage (switching out immediately upon entering Fluttering Frock state is the fastest possible method to do this).

 When it comes to combos, Vivian can use any combination of skills that generate 2 or 3 Flight Feathers to reach a total of 4 or 5 to ultimately convert. Make sure not to waste any Flight Feathers however, as you would lose potential Abloom activations otherwise, so only use Ultimate on Vivian if she’s devoid of these resources.
 Regarding her position in the meta, Vivian is an Agent who is heavily dependent on other Anomaly Agents’ Anomaly DMG and Anomaly Proficiency stats to perform. She is capable of dishing out amazing Anomaly DMG in the right team, whether that is through Corruption, Disorder, or Abloom. Generally speaking, all 3 of these damage sources, on top of the damage provided during her on-field time, make her stand out as a comfortable high to top tier character who is able to slot in any Anomaly Agent’s team and perform at least decently well to very effectively, especially if that Anomaly Agent is meant to stay on the field during the majority of combat. Check out our Teams section for a more in-depth look on this!
 Generally speaking, Vivian is an Agent who’s simple to play and build, who can perform very well in low-cost teams and with a low-cost W-Engine, which doesn’t require a lot of premium resources put into them. She, however, does hold some big vertical upgrades that can be considered to enhance team performance if necessary. Her main weakness is undoubtedly her reliance on Assist Follow-Ups to have the highest possible Flight Feather generation, as well as adapting her combos dynamically based on the amount of Flight Feathers you can generate and convert in the moment. Additionally, Vivian’s damage isn’t just dependent on her stats but other characters’ which means everyone in the team will require good investment in terms of Disc Drives . However if players can manage this, they will find a lot of success with Vivian as she is one of this game’s top-performing Anomaly Agents.
 To summarize, Vivian is an Anomaly DPS Agent that lots of players can draw high performance out of. Pairing her with a second Anomaly Agent is mandatory for her to reach her full potential, but she has lots of options to cover for this, meaning building a team around her is not difficult. She sports great damage with dynamic combos and is able to buff any Anomaly Agent’s damage to great lengths, all of these factors securing her a high spot in the Zenless Zone Zero meta.

sections.heading: Rotations
sections.text: Vivian's rotations are dynamic depending on the enemy you're fighting, the resources you have available (Decibels, Chain Attacks, EX Specials, Assist Points...) and your 2 other party members. However, we listed below some possible combos to help you build Flight Feathers from 0 to 4 or 5 and quickly convert them into Guard Feathers to activate her Ablooms as fast as possible.Note: Chain Attack can replace any Defensive Assist + Assist Follow-Up or Noblewoman - Waltz if available. It's also possible in very rare cases to Chain twice into Vivian to perform a 4 Flying Feather combo only using 2 Chain Attacks, however other teammates may want to execute Chain Attacks instead.IMPORTANT: If Vivian has any Guard Feathers, only use EX Specials on any character if an Attribute Anomaly is present on the enemy! Otherwise, Abloom will not activate and the Guard Feather will be wasted.

sections.heading: Synergy
sections.text:
Below we list only the most important synergies for Vivian . The character can work with others if you know what to do and how to use them.

 Miyabi Yanagi Alice Jane Doe Piper Grace - Vivian functions very well with all the Anomaly DPS Agents we have in the game. They activate Vivian's Additional Ability and her damage scales directly off of how much Anomaly damage her teammates do. For this reason, Miyabi is the odd one out of the bunch as a lot of her damage comes from CRIT instead of Anomaly, however she still deals enough Anomaly DMG to make a viable pairing. Overall, all of Vivian's best teams involve Anomaly DPS Agents as they increase each other's damage, making these pairings highly recommended.
 Astra Yao Yuzuha Nicole Lucy - These 4 generalist Support units are capable of servicing as the Support to any team in the game. Astra Yao provides Quick Assists, extra Chain Attacks, healing, super low field time, ATK, DMG and CRIT DMG buffs which makes her one of the strongest overall choices. Astra Yao also helps tremendously with consuming Guard Feathers for Vivian to dish out her damage faster. Yuzuha is the ultimate Anomaly buffer, surpassing Astra Yao in those teams, who also has awesome ATK and DMG% buffs applicable to any Agent as well, giving her strong general use potential; Nicole provides the sought-after DEF Shred and Ether DMG Boost via her Additional Ability. Nicole and Astra Yao are particularly appreciated due to helping Vivian activate Corruption. Lastly, Lucy has long-lasting ATK buffs which makes her a very practical choice, and she ends up being preferable when needed to activate Additional Abilities of certain characters. All in all, these four can work with any team in the game to great effect.

 Review

 Ratings
 This tier list assesses Agents (characters) based on their combat potential in Zenless Zone Zero's most demanding contents - Deadly Assault (DA) and Shiyu Defense (SD) . Please keep in mind Zenless Zone Zero is a skill-based game and each character has a different playstyle, difficulty level and even special tricks and combos. Zenless Zone Zero is also a team based game and it's only by combining both these factors to the highest level a character can reach optimal performance.

 Anomaly DPS
 T1
 Endgame Modes

 Pros & Cons
 Pros
 Damage scales directly with Anomaly DPS strength — the more Anomaly damage your DPS does, the better she becomes;

 Great team flexibility with many strong and viable synergies;

 Very capable F2P W-Engine option.

 Cons
 Potential damage can suffer if your other anomaly characters aren't sufficiently invested into;

 Relies on Perfect Assists to make the best use of her kit, making her enemy-dependent to an extent,

 Review
 Vivian is an Ether S-Rank Anomaly Agent whose defining characteristic is her ability to apply extra Anomaly damage based on your other Agents’ Anomaly damage. This element alone makes her fit into several teams and have high flexibility as a Sub-DPS type Agent, it defines the majority of her damage potential and is what her gameplay revolves around. Let’s first explain her kit and mechanics (fair warning: this will be lengthy).
 These “extra Anomalies” (to use simple terms) are called “Abloom”. Vivian triggers Abloom whenever a character is suffering from any Attribute Anomaly of the 5 standard elements (Ether, Electric, Fire, Ice, Physical) and any character in the team uses their EX Special, once per ability used. Simultaneously, Basic Attack: “Featherbloom” is triggered. Featherbloom and Abloom both can activate off-field via any party member’s EX Special attack. This process can also happen whenever any Attribute Anomaly of the 5 elemental kinds is inflicted on an enemy once every 0.5s while her Additional Ability is active. However, in both cases this must come at the cost of 1 “Guard Feather” each time, which Vivian needs to generate on-field in several ways.
 Generating a Guard Feather requires first converting it from a “Flight Feather”. Any available Flight Feathers, up to a maximum of 5, are converted into Guard Feathers via Vivian’s Basic Attack in the “Fluttering Frock” state during which she is suspended in mid-air. Fluttering Frock is activated if any Flight Feathers are available and in the following ways:
 Holding Basic Attack after using Basic Attack 4, Dodge Counter or Quick Assist;

 Using her Noblewoman - Waltz Basic attack (we cover this shortly after);

 Using an EX Special attack, Assist Follow-Up, Chain Attack or Ultimate.

 Holding Dodge cancels the state if it’s undesirable, and can additionally prevent Vivian from causing her to enter this state at all. If at any point Vivian switches out during the Fluttering Frock state, it automatically activates “Suspension” which is the attack responsible for converting Flight Feathers into Guard Feathers. Noblewoman - Waltz is a Basic Attack only available after pressing Basic Attack in the Noblewoman state, during which Vivian gets a free dodge once (which doesn’t give a Dodge Counter). It can be accessed in the following ways:
 After using Basic Attack 4, Dodge Counter or Quick Assist.

 To generate Flight Feathers, which are necessary to convert into Guard Feathers for Vivian to use and trigger Abloom, different abilities give different amounts in the following ways:
 1 Flight Feather after using Noblewoman - Waltz (this gives 1 additional Feather if it triggers a Perfect Dodge);

 2 Flight Feathers after using Chain Attack;

 2 Flight Feathers after using Assist Follow-Up;

 3 Flight Feathers after using EX Special attack;

 5 Flight Feathers after using Ultimate.

 All of these abilities are reliant on Energy of some kind or are slow to access consistently (Noblewoman - Waltz). This means Assist Follow-Ups are especially important to generate Flight Feathers with Vivian. Upon converting available Flight Feathers by using Basic Attack in the Fluttering Frock state (called “Suspension”), Vivian is free to switch out to other characters for them to apply Attribute Anomalies for Vivian to trigger Abloom with.
 Vivian’s Core Passive is responsible for triggering Abloom, and hence it is the top priority to focus on to maximize Vivian’s damage. It has the following effects
 When first engaging in combat, gain 2 Flight Feathers.

 When Basic Attack: Featherbloom hits a target inflicted with an Attribute Anomaly, trigger Abloom which deals damage depending on the Anomaly Proficiency of the inflicted Attribute Anomaly applied to the enemy, as well as the element of the Anomaly (balanced to give out the same damage roughly).

 When Suspension or Featherbloom hit targets suffering any Attribute Anomaly, inflict a Damage Over Time effect called “Vivian’s Prophecy” which deals Ether DMG based on her ATK every 0.55s. This contributes to Anomaly DMG and ends when targets aren’t affected by Anomalies.

 Additional Ability: Corruption and Corruption Disorder DMG increases by 15%. Vivian now also consumes 1 Guard Feather and triggers Featherbloom (and Abloom) up to once every 0.5s when any Attribute Anomaly is inflicted on an enemy.

 Beyond the effects of all abilities listed above, all of Vivian’s combat skills inflict DMG and Daze as normal. Some are Physical DMG, but most are Ether DMG. It is important to level Vivian’s combat skills to an extent for extra Daze output to generate more Stun windows for your team on most enemies, even though only her Core Passive contributes to her Abloom DMG.
 Based on this kit, the game plan with Vivian is therefore as follows:
 Generate up to 5 Flight Feathers in any way (4 is fine depending on the team & available resources);

 Enter Fluttering Frock state;

 Switch out to automatically convert Flight Feathers into Guard Feathers and apply Anomalies to trigger Abloom for lots of Anomaly damage (switching out immediately upon entering Fluttering Frock state is the fastest possible method to do this).

 When it comes to combos, Vivian can use any combination of skills that generate 2 or 3 Flight Feathers to reach a total of 4 or 5 to ultimately convert. Make sure not to waste any Flight Feathers however, as you would lose potential Abloom activations otherwise, so only use Ultimate on Vivian if she’s devoid of these resources.
 Regarding her position in the meta, Vivian is an Agent who is heavily dependent on other Anomaly Agents’ Anomaly DMG and Anomaly Proficiency stats to perform. She is capable of dishing out amazing Anomaly DMG in the right team, whether that is through Corruption, Disorder, or Abloom. Generally speaking, all 3 of these damage sources, on top of the damage provided during her on-field time, make her stand out as a comfortable high to top tier character who is able to slot in any Anomaly Agent’s team and perform at least decently well to very effectively, especially if that Anomaly Agent is meant to stay on the field during the majority of combat. Check out our Teams section for a more in-depth look on this!
 Generally speaking, Vivian is an Agent who’s simple to play and build, who can perform very well in low-cost teams and with a low-cost W-Engine, which doesn’t require a lot of premium resources put into them. She, however, does hold some big vertical upgrades that can be considered to enhance team performance if necessary. Her main weakness is undoubtedly her reliance on Assist Follow-Ups to have the highest possible Flight Feather generation, as well as adapting her combos dynamically based on the amount of Flight Feathers you can generate and convert in the moment. Additionally, Vivian’s damage isn’t just dependent on her stats but other characters’ which means everyone in the team will require good investment in terms of Disc Drives . However if players can manage this, they will find a lot of success with Vivian as she is one of this game’s top-performing Anomaly Agents.
 To summarize, Vivian is an Anomaly DPS Agent that lots of players can draw high performance out of. Pairing her with a second Anomaly Agent is mandatory for her to reach her full potential, but she has lots of options to cover for this, meaning building a team around her is not difficult. She sports great damage with dynamic combos and is able to buff any Anomaly Agent’s damage to great lengths, all of these factors securing her a high spot in the Zenless Zone Zero meta.

 Synergy
 Below we list only the most important synergies for Vivian . The character can work with others if you know what to do and how to use them.

 Miyabi Yanagi Alice Jane Doe Piper Grace - Vivian functions very well with all the Anomaly DPS Agents we have in the game. They activate Vivian's Additional Ability and her damage scales directly off of how much Anomaly damage her teammates do. For this reason, Miyabi is the odd one out of the bunch as a lot of her damage comes from CRIT instead of Anomaly, however she still deals enough Anomaly DMG to make a viable pairing. Overall, all of Vivian's best teams involve Anomaly DPS Agents as they increase each other's damage, making these pairings highly recommended.
 Astra Yao Yuzuha Nicole Lucy - These 4 generalist Support units are capable of servicing as the Support to any team in the game. Astra Yao provides Quick Assists, extra Chain Attacks, healing, super low field time, ATK, DMG and CRIT DMG buffs which makes her one of the strongest overall choices. Astra Yao also helps tremendously with consuming Guard Feathers for Vivian to dish out her damage faster. Yuzuha is the ultimate Anomaly buffer, surpassing Astra Yao in those teams, who also has awesome ATK and DMG% buffs applicable to any Agent as well, giving her strong general use potential; Nicole provides the sought-after DEF Shred and Ether DMG Boost via her Additional Ability. Nicole and Astra Yao are particularly appreciated due to helping Vivian activate Corruption. Lastly, Lucy has long-lasting ATK buffs which makes her a very practical choice, and she ends up being preferable when needed to activate Additional Abilities of certain characters. All in all, these four can work with any team in the game to great effect.
